claims.explanation: TW-37 is a BH3-mimetic that binds BCL2, BCL-XL, and MCL1, so selectivity likely reflects which anti-apoptotic BCL2-family proteins the tumor depends on. Lines with high MCL1 or BCL2/BCL2L1 expression and intact apoptotic signaling should be sensitized, whereas lines with low dependence on these targets or with alternative survival signaling (e.g., strong MAPK/EGFR/PI3K-driven resistance) are protected. The observed enrichment of TP53 mutations in both sensitive and resistant lines suggests p53 status alone is not the main determinant; instead, the balance of BCL2-family dependence and apoptotic priming drives the pattern.

features.basis: TW-37 binds MCL1 with high affinity (Ki 260 nM) and MCL1 dependence is a known resistance node in melanoma and solid tumors
TW-37 was designed to target the BH3-binding groove of BCL2 and binds BCL2 with high affinity (Ki 290 nM)
TW-37 binds BCL-XL (Ki 1110 nM) and BCL-XL is a pro-survival factor in senescent and tumor cells
TP53 mutations are common in both sensitive and resistant lines, but p53 loss can impair apoptotic priming and reduce BH3-mimetic response
BRAF-mutant melanoma lines show ERK-independent MCL1 expression that mediates resistance to MEK inhibition and BH3-mimetics
EGFR-driven survival signaling can maintain anti-apoptotic tone and limit BH3-mimetic killing
PI3K pathway activation supports survival and is enriched in less-affected lines
PTEN loss activates PI3K/AKT survival signaling, reducing dependence on BCL2-family inhibition
NF1 loss activates RAS/MAPK signaling, which can upregulate MCL1 and other anti-apoptotic proteins
KRAS mutations are present in several resistant lines and activate MAPK/PI3K survival pathways
CDKN2A loss is common in resistant lines and may reflect a broader oncogenic program with alternative survival dependencies
ARID1A mutations appear in several sensitive lines and may alter chromatin state and apoptotic priming
